Rashi on Arakhin 33a:11:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - מהיכא תיתי דלא יצאו ביובל? הלא הוקשו לשדה אחוזה, ולמאי אצטריך "וביובל יצא":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:11:1.english: What is [he] saying - From where would it enter [one's mind] that they do not go out [of the buyer's possession] in the Jubilee? Were they not compared to an ancestral field? And why is [the phrase] "and in the Jubilee it shall go out" needed?

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:11:2.english: And the Jubilee [Year] arrived in the second year - of the purchase of this [person] who bought it from the [Temple] treasurer:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:12:1.hebrew: ללוקח הוי - דהכי תניא לעיל: גאלה אחר מיד הקדש, הגיע היובל ולא נגאלה, היה חלוט לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:12:1.english: It belongs to the buyer - For so it was taught above: [If] another [person] redeemed it from the possession of the Temple treasury, [and] the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed [by the original owner], it becomes permanently his:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:12:2.hebrew: לכהנים נפקא - דהמקדיש שדה אחוזה וגאלה אחר, יוצאה לכהנים ביובל. ולהכי נקט רב הונא "שנה שניה", דאי פגע יובל בשנה ראשונה, לא אצטריך "וביובל יצא", דכי מדמית ליה לבתי ערי חומה — אכתי לא איחלט ליה, ונפיק ביובל, דהא יש לו כח יפה שבשדות:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:12:2.english: It leaves to the priests - For if one consecrates an ancestral field and another redeems it, it leaves to [the possession of] the priests in the Jubilee. And for this reason [Rav Huna] specified "the second year": for if [the Jubilee] arrived in the first year, [the phrase] "and it shall go out in the Jubilee" would not be necessary, because [even] if you compare it to houses of walled cities, it has not yet become permanently [the buyer's], and it goes out in the Jubilee, since it has the greater power of fields:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:13:1.hebrew: אפילו לא גאלו - אחר, נמי ליפוק מיד הקדש, דהא כתיב "וביובל יצא", דלא אצטריך למכתב משום מכר הדיוט, דהא אתקש לשדות:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:13:1.english: Even [if] he did not redeem it - [meaning] another [person], it should also go out from the possession of the Temple treasury, for it is written: "and in the Jubilee it shall go out"; for it was not necessary to write [this] regarding an ordinary sale, since it is compared to fields:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:14:1.hebrew: בן לוי יפה כחו בממכרו - שגואל מיד, שדה מגרש עריהם ובתי ערי חומה גואלין לעולם, ויוצאין ביובל, כדאמר לקמן:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:14:1.english: A Levite's power is enhanced with regard to his sale - for he may redeem immediately; the fields of the open land of their cities and the houses of walled cities they may redeem forever, and they go out [to their owners] in the Jubilee, as it states later:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:14:2.hebrew: הורע כחו בהקדישו - שלא יוצא בלא פדיון, כדמפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:14:2.english: His power is diminished with regard to his consecration - That it does not leave [the possession of the Temple treasury] without redemption, as [the Gemara] explains below:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:15:1.hebrew: ויצא ממכר - אי הוה כתיב "ואשר יגאל מן הלוים ויצא ממכר ביובל", ולא הוה כתב "בית", הוה אמינא: אפילו שטרי ומטלטלין של לוי, אם מכרן, יוצאין לו ביובל:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:15:1.english: “That was sold…shall go out” - Had it been written, “And if one purchases from the Levites, that which was sold shall go out in the Jubilee,” and it had not written “house,” I would have said: even promissory notes and movable property of a Levite, if he sold them, go out [back] to him in the Jubilee:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:17:1.hebrew: ופליגא דרבי אושעיא - הא דאמר רב הונא לעיל: מקדיש בית בבתי חצרים וגאלה אחר מיד הקדש, יוצאה מידו וחוזרת לבעלים ביובל — פליגא אדרבי אושעיא:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:17:1.english: And it disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya - That which Rav Huna said above — [namely, that if] one consecrates a house among houses of [unwalled] courtyards and another redeems it from the possession of the Temple treasury, it leaves his possession and returns to the [original] owners in the Jubilee [Year] — disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:17:2.hebrew: בכלל ונתן הכסף וקם לו - שהלוקח כלום מיד הקדש, יקום המקח בידו לעולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:17:2.english: Included in "And he will give the money and it will be assured to him" - [meaning] that one who purchases anything from the possession of the consecrated treasury [hekdesh], the purchase remains in his possession forever:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:18:1.hebrew: כשפרט לך הכתוב - בגואל שדה אחוזה של אחרים מיד הקדש, דיוצאה מידו ומתחלקת — האי הוא דאפקיה רחמנא בהדיא מכלל "ונתן הכסף וקם לו":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:18:1.english: When the verse specified for you - regarding one who redeems another's ancestral field from the Temple treasury, that it leaves his possession and is divided [among the priests] — it is this that the Merciful One explicitly excluded from the general rule of "and he shall give the money, and it shall be established as his":

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:18:2.hebrew: אבל הנך - בתי החצרים, כדקיימי קיימי בכלל "וקם לו", ולא נפקא מידא דלוקח:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:18:2.english: But these - [i.e.,] the houses in [unwalled] courtyards, remain in their [current] status, included in [the verse] "and it shall be his," and do not leave the possession of the buyer:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:19:1.hebrew: וביובל יצא - לרבי אושעיא ל"ל:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:19:1.english: And in the Jubilee it shall go out - According to Rabbi Oshaya, why do I [need it]?

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:1:1.hebrew: הניחא לרבנן - דפליגי עליה דר' יהודה [דאמרי] שנת חמשים אינה ממנין השמיטין, אצטריך לממני יובלות כדקאמרת:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:1:1.english: This works out well according to the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda, [who say] that the fiftieth year is not [included] in the count of the Sabbatical years — it was necessary to count Jubilee years, as you said:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:1:2.hebrew: אלא לרבי יהודה דאמר שנת חמשים - הויא שנת יובל ועולה נמי למנין שמיטה הבאה, ל"ל לממני יובלות? בשמיטין סגיא — משבע לשבע שנים יעשו שמיטה לעולם, שאין שנה מפסקת בנתיים, ואין כאן שום טעות:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:1:2.english: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says [that] the fiftieth year - is the Jubilee Year and is also counted toward the reckoning of the following Sabbatical [cycle], why do I [need] to count Jubilees? [Counting] by Sabbatical [years] is enough — every seven years they should observe a Sabbatical [year] forever, since there is no intervening year in between, and there is no error here:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:1:3.hebrew: ודאי - דקתני לעיל "מנו שמיטין ויובלות בימי עזרא", דלא כר' יהודה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:1:3.english: Certainly - [that] which it teaches above, "they counted Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years in the days of Ezra," is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:20:1.hebrew: השלמה בעי - להשלים לו שנה אחת משתי שנים שהיא ראויה לשהות ביד לוקח, כדתניא לעיל בריש פירקין: "אכלה שנה אחת לפני היובל, משלימין לו שנה אחרת לאחר היובל":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:20:1.english: It requires completion - to complete for him one year of the two years that it is fit to remain in the buyer's possession, as it was taught earlier at the beginning of our chapter: "If he consumed [its produce] for one year before the Jubilee, they complete for him another year after the Jubilee":

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב הונא גרסינן - כרב הונא דאמר לעיל: מקדיש בית בבתי החצרים, וגאלה אחר מיד מקדיש, יוצאה לבעלים ביובל:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:1.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav Huna — [this is] our reading [of the text]: in accordance with Rav Huna, who said above: [If] one consecrates a house among the houses of unwalled courtyards, and another [person] redeems it from the possession of the consecrator, it goes out to the [original] owner in the Jubilee [Year]:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:2.english: And [it is] a conclusive refutation of Rabbi Oshaya - who said [that] they remain as they are in the possession of the buyer:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:3.hebrew: וגואלו לעולם - ואפילו גאלה אחר, גואלה מידו, ולא הויא כשדה אחוזה, דכתיב בה: "לא יגאל עוד":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:3.english: And he may redeem it always - And even if another [person] redeemed it [from the Temple treasury], [the original owner] may redeem it from his hand; and it is not like an ancestral field, concerning which it is written: "it shall not be redeemed any more."

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:4.hebrew: גאלה אחר מיד הקדש והגיע יובל ולא גאלה - מקדיש מידו, חוזרת לו בחנם:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:21:4.english: [If] another redeemed it from the possession of the Temple treasury, and the Jubilee arrived and he did not redeem it - [meaning] the consecrator [did not redeem it] from his hand, it returns to him for free:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:2:1.english: And [did] they not count Jubilees - in the days of Sennacherib:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:2:2.english: But isn't it written - [This was said] in [the time of] Zedekiah:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:3:1.hebrew: מקץ שבע שנים תשלחו וגו' והוינן בה מקץ שבע שנים - משמע לאחר שבע שנים, שאף שנה שביעית עובד, והא כתיב "ועבדך שש שנים":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:3:1.english: "At the end of seven years you shall let go, etc." And we discussed it: "At the end of seven years" - [This] implies after seven years, [meaning] that even [during] the seventh year [he serves]; yet isn't it written, "and he shall serve you six years"?

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:3:2.hebrew: שש לנמכר - כדכתי' (שמות כ״א:ב׳) "שש שנים יעבד":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:3:2.english: Six [years] for one who is sold - as it is written (Exodus 21:2), "Six years shall he serve":

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:3:3.hebrew: ושבע לנרצע - שהנרצע אינו יוצא עד היובל, ואם נרצע ופגע יובל בשנה שמינית לרציעתו, יוצא ביובל. אלמא בימי צדקיה הוה יובל, וצדקיהו בימי חורבן הבית, דהוו כמה וכמה דורות אחר גלות סנחריב:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:3:3.english: And seven for one whose ear was pierced - For one whose ear was pierced does not go free until the Jubilee, and if his ear was pierced and the Jubilee occurred in the eighth year of his piercing, he goes free in the Jubilee. Evidently, in the days of Zedekiah the Jubilee was [in effect], and Zedekiah [lived] in the days of the destruction of the Temple, which was many generations after the exile of Sennacherib:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:4:1.hebrew: בתוכחה כתיב - דקא מוכח להו ירמיה, וקאמר להו: "השלחתם באותן שנים שהייתם חייבים לשלח":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:4:1.english: It is written in reproof - For Jeremiah is rebuking them and saying to them: "Did you send [them] free in those years when you were obligated to send [them] free?"

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:5:1.hebrew: דכתיב - בימי צדקיהו: "כי המוכר אל הממכר לא ישוב", דקאמר להו: סופכם לגלות ויהא יובל בטל, ולא יחזרו שדות לבעליהן:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:5:1.english: As it is written - in the days of Zedekiah: "For the seller shall not return to that which he has sold," [meaning] that he [Ezekiel] says to them: "Ultimately you will be exiled, and the Jubilee will be nullified, and fields will not return to their owners":

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:5:2.hebrew: אפשר יובל בטל - משגלו שבט ראובן וגד, ונביא מתנבא עליו וכו':
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:5:2.english: Is it possible [that] the Jubilee was nullified - once the tribe of Reuben and Gad were exiled, and [yet] a prophet prophesies about it, etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:7:1.hebrew: מה טיבו של יאשיהו בבית אל - דהא קרא ביאשיהו כתיב, כשהיה חוזר לבער עבודת כוכבים שבארץ ישראל, ובית אל של מלכי ישראל היתה, ויאשיהו מלך יהודה מה טיבו בה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:7:1.english: What business does Josiah have in Bethel - For the verse is written regarding Josiah, when he was going around to eradicate idolatry in the Land of Israel; and Bethel belonged to the kings of Israel, so what business did Josiah, king of Judah, have there?

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:7:2.hebrew: קציר - קצין, דנו"ן מתחלפת ברי"ש, כדכתיב: "נבוכד נצר", "נבוכד ראצר":
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:7:2.english: Katzir [harvest] - [This means] katzin [a ruler], for [the letter] nun interchanges with [the letter] reish, as it is written: "Nebuchadnezzar" [and] "Nebuchadrezzar":

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:8:1.english: Houses of the courtyards - [Houses in] towns that do not have a wall:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:8:2.hebrew: כח יפה - כדמפרש: נגאלין מיד, ואין צריך להמתין שני שנים ביד הלוקח, והיינו כבתים של ערי חומה:
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:8:2.english: The advantageous provision - As [the Mishnah] explains: they are redeemed immediately, and one does not need to wait two years [while the property remains] in the possession of the buyer, and this is like houses of walled cities:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:8:3.hebrew: ובגרעון כסף - שמנכה לו הלוקח לפי שנים ששהו בידו, כשדות, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:כ״ז): "וחשב את שני ממכרו" וגו':
Rashi on Arakhin 33a:8:3.english: And with a deduction [from the] money - that the buyer deducts for him [from the redemption price] according to the years that [the houses] remained in his possession, like fields, as it is written (Leviticus 25:27): "And he shall calculate the years of his sale," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:9:1.english: Shall be reckoned with the fields of the country - [This] is written regarding the houses of the courtyards:

Rashi on Arakhin 33a:9:2.english: And with a deduction from the money - [That is,] if he comes to redeem them before the Jubilee:

Tosafot on Arakhin 33a:5:1.hebrew: אלא מלמד שהחזירן ירמיה ויאשיה מלך עליהם - ותימה, שהרי אחרי שהחזירן ירמיה לא עמדו בארץ קודם חורבן כ"א ל"ו שנה, כדפרישית לעיל בפ"ב (ערכין דף יב:), וא"כ לא הגיעו עד היובל, והיאך נוכל למצוא "וישמעו וישלחו"? וי"ל דנוכל למצוא אותם עבדים שהיו להם קודם שגלו. והא דפריך לעיל: והכתיב "וישמעו וישלחו" — עיקר הפירכא מדכתיב (ירמיהו ל״ד:י׳) "וישמעו כל השרים וכל העם אשר באו בברית", משמע שנכנסו בברית לשלח עבדיהם חפשים ביובל כשיגיע היובל:
Tosafot on Arakhin 33a:5:1.english: Rather, this teaches that Jeremiah brought them back, and Josiah ruled over them - And this is astonishing: for after Jeremiah brought them back, they did not remain in the land before the destruction [of the Temple] except for thirty-six years, as I explained above in the second chapter (Arakhin 12b). If so, they did not reach the Jubilee, so how could we find [a fulfillment of] "And they listened and let them go"? And one can say that we can find [this regarding] those slaves whom they had before they were exiled. And as for that which [the Gemara] asks above, "But isn't it written: 'And they listened and let them go'?" — the main point of the difficulty is from what is written (Jeremiah 34:10): "And all the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant listened," which implies that they entered into a covenant to send their slaves free in the Jubilee, when the Jubilee would arrive:
